key_insight: Common guidance heuristics (e.g., CFG) ignore the geometry of the learned generative manifold and break probability conservation; by analyzing guidance through the continuity equation, the paper derives a corrected flow-based guidance that preserves probability mass and keeps samples on the manifold.
problem_solved: Heuristic linear combinations of scores/velocities used for conditional guidance drive samples off the learned manifold and violate probability conservation, especially under strong guidance, leading to degraded or unstable synthesis.
method: Formulate conditional guidance in terms of the continuity equation to reveal how guidance perturbs probability flow and introduces divergence.
Derive a probability-conserving correction (a divergence-aware / manifold-aware modification) to standard flow/diffusion guidance that enforces mass conservation.
Integrate the correction into flow-based guidance pipelines, replacing extrapolative CFG-like operations with geometry-preserving updates.
impact: Enables stronger, more reliable conditioning in diffusion and flow models without breaking the model's learned distribution—practical for higher-fidelity synthesis and safer, more predictable guided generation.
visual_elements: Diagram of a generative manifold with vector fields: (a) standard CFG pushing samples off-manifold, (b) probability-conserving flow guidance keeping flows tangent to the manifold.
Schematic of the continuity equation showing probability density, velocity field, and divergence terms with the corrective term highlighted.
Before/after sample grids or nearest-neighbour manifold projections illustrating improved fidelity and reduced off-manifold artifacts under strong guidance.
Heatmap/plot of divergence or probability mass over time comparing heuristic guidance vs. probability-conserving guidance.
paper_authors: Parsa Esmati, Junha Hyung, Amirhossein Dadashzadeh, Jaegul Choo, Majid Mirmehdi
